M3_sequential_benchmark.description: 5 conditions x 5 sequential tasks on hydra_mesh
M3_sequential_benchmark.key_finding: Condition E (structural graph memory, no text) achieves 100% success at 115.5s avg — 15.4% faster than static graph (136.5s) and 36.1% faster than graph+text (180.7s)

M4_failure_aware_benchmark.description: 5 conditions x 4 diagnostic tasks on hydra_mesh

ABLATION_NO_ATTR_FILTER.note: Catastrophic failure: penalizing all edges in failed trajectory destroys valid navigation paths

ABLATION_NO_RECENCY_DECAY.note: Stale penalty poisoning: permanent penalties impair recovery

M4_failure_aware_benchmark.key_finding: Adding negative experience to positive priors reduces tool calls by 14.8% (6.75->5.75) and execution time by 12.6% (132.0s->115.4s). Ablation 1 (no attribution filter) collapses to 0% success — proving causal attribution is essential.

cross_experiment_conclusions: Graph-guided pre-retrieval is necessary and sufficient for 100% task success on scaled repos (59 files). Stateless baseline fails at 50-60%.
Structural graph memory (Condition E) achieves identical accuracy to narrative text memory (Condition C) with 15-36% lower latency across both M3 and M4 benchmarks.
Causal attribution filtering is not optional: removing it (Ablation 1) causes 0% success — indiscriminate edge penalization is worse than no memory.
Task-conditioned modulation prevents cross-module interference: T4 rate-limiter edge utilization = 0% on unrelated transformer task.
Cold-start property verified: at T1 (empty overlay), Condition E behavior is provably identical to Condition B (static graph).
Zero stale-memory regressions across all 45 task runs (9 tasks x 5 conditions).
